document_title: Preventing suicide: a resource for filmmakers and others working on stage and screen
clause: Show overcoming a suicidal crisis, help-seeking, looking after oneself and others, and messages of hope.

document_title: Preventing suicide: a resource for filmmakers and others working on stage and screen
clause: Avoid portrayals that nurture myths or misunderstandings; account for possible imitation effects among vulnerable viewers.

document_title: Preventing suicide: a resource for filmmakers and others working on stage and screen
clause: Portrayals of suicide on stage and screen can have imitation effects, while portrayals that focus on overcoming a suicidal crisis can reduce suicide risk.

document_title: Preventing suicide: a resource for filmmakers and others working on stage and screen
clause: Use the opportunity a storyline offers to highlight the importance of seeking help and to provide messages of hope.

publisher: National Action Alliance for Suicide Prevention
document_title: National Recommendations for Depicting Suicide
clause: Avoid showing or describing details about suicide methods, including graphic depictions of how someone took their life, as such portrayals can increase imitation.

publisher: National Action Alliance for Suicide Prevention
document_title: National Recommendations for Depicting Suicide
clause: Convey that suicide is complex and often caused by a range of factors, rather than by a single event.

publisher: National Action Alliance for Suicide Prevention
document_title: National Recommendations for Depicting Suicide
clause: Show that help is available: consider conveying a character choosing to seek help, such as calling or texting a crisis line, reaching out to a professional or to social supports, or finding alternative coping strategies.

publisher: National Action Alliance for Suicide Prevention
document_title: National Recommendations for Depicting Suicide
clause: Consult with suicide prevention messaging experts and people with personal experience, who can help craft more authentic storylines.

publisher: National Action Alliance for Suicide Prevention
document_title: National Recommendations for Depicting Suicide
clause: Portray characters with suicidal thoughts who do not go on to die by suicide; stories of survival and healing woven into scripts provide hope and a balanced perspective.

publisher: National Action Alliance for Suicide Prevention
document_title: National Recommendations for Depicting Suicide
clause: Portray everyday characters who can be a lifeline: most crises are time-limited, so consider depicting a character who kept someone safe or supported them until that time passed.

publisher: National Action Alliance for Suicide Prevention
document_title: National Recommendations for Depicting Suicide
clause: Depict the grieving and healing process of people who lose someone to suicide, focusing on how friends, family, and support groups offered solace and support.

publisher: National Action Alliance for Suicide Prevention
document_title: National Recommendations for Depicting Suicide
clause: Connect viewers to resources: highlight help-seeking resources such as the 988 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline (call or text 988) through the program and its promotion.

document_title: Guidance on depictions of suicide and self-harm in drama and film
clause: Signpost viewers to appropriate sources of support, such as Samaritans' helpline, at the end of programmes covering suicide or self-harm, to encourage help-seeking.

document_title: Guidance on depictions of suicide and self-harm in drama and film
clause: Samaritans' Media Advice team works closely with drama producers, providing advice and a script review service.

document_title: Guidance on depictions of suicide and self-harm in drama and film
clause: In any portrayal of a suicide or suicide attempt, give as little detail as possible about the method used; for example, do not name or show the type or quantity of tablets consumed.

document_title: Guidance on depictions of suicide and self-harm in drama and film
clause: Avoid giving details of how the means of suicide were obtained, for example describing an instrument as easily and cheaply obtained online.

document_title: Guidance on depictions of suicide and self-harm in drama and film
clause: Portraying a suicide as easy, quick, peaceful or pain-free can influence a person's decision to make an attempt; avoid it, and avoid introducing new, unusual or particularly lethal methods into public consciousness.

document_title: Guidance on depictions of suicide and self-harm in drama and film
clause: It is risky to indicate any reward following a suicide death or attempt, such as separated parents reuniting or bullies being shamed; a death by suicide should never be described as a release, setting a person free, or providing peace.

document_title: Guidance on depictions of suicide and self-harm in drama and film
clause: Convey the complexity of suicidal behaviour and avoid simplistic explanations that attribute an attempt or death to a single incident such as losing a job or a relationship breakdown.

document_title: Guidance on depictions of suicide and self-harm in drama and film
clause: Sensitive storylines that depict a character overcoming a crisis and show hopeful recovery can encourage people suffering in silence to reach out for help, particularly if the character seeks help and chooses to live (the Papageno effect).

document_title: Guidance on depictions of suicide and self-harm in drama and film
clause: Avoid overly dramatising a suicide, as this can romanticise or glorify the behaviour and inadvertently promote it to people who may be vulnerable.

document_title: Guidance on depictions of suicide and self-harm in drama and film
clause: Portraying self-harm may contribute to its normalisation, particularly with young audiences; consider the details included and avoid repeated or excessive coverage.

document_title: Guidance on depictions of suicide and self-harm in drama and film
clause: Avoid portraying a suicide attempt as something that can quickly be recovered from, such as a character returning to normal life within hours or days.

document_title: Guidance on depictions of suicide and self-harm in drama and film
clause: Consider content warnings at the start of key episodes so viewers can choose whether to watch, and keep suicide methods and locations out of publicity images.

document_title: Mental ill-health and suicide: A Mindframe resource for stage and screen
clause: Preferred portrayals do not provide visual details of, or spoken references to, the exact method; detailed portrayal of particular methods has been linked to copycat suicides by that method.

document_title: Mental ill-health and suicide: A Mindframe resource for stage and screen
clause: Ask whether the portrayal might be wrongly interpreted as a solution to a problem, and whether the music, lighting or setting romanticises or glamorises suicide.

document_title: Mental ill-health and suicide: A Mindframe resource for stage and screen
clause: Including phone numbers and contact details for support services at the end of a piece, or as part of the drama, provides immediate support for those who may be distressed or prompted to seek help.

document_title: Mental ill-health and suicide: A Mindframe resource for stage and screen
clause: Depictions that emphasise consequences for others and sources of support for vulnerable viewers may encourage people to seek help; showing the impact on family, friends and community places the death in a broader context of loss.

document_title: Mental ill-health and suicide: A Mindframe resource for stage and screen
clause: If suicide is portrayed, consider the length of the depiction and whether less detail would have a better dramatic effect than a graphic depiction; a succession of stories about suicide can normalise it as an acceptable course of action.

document_title: Mental ill-health and suicide: A Mindframe resource for stage and screen
clause: Consider including a content warning stating that the program, film or show includes depictions of suicide or mental ill-health.

document_title: Mental ill-health and suicide: A Mindframe resource for stage and screen
clause: Access reliable information and expert opinion about suicide, and consider the value of talking to people directly affected by suicide when developing storylines.

clause: Do tell others considering suicide how they can get help, and present suicide as mainly arising from treatable illness, and thus preventable.

clause: Don't accept single-reason explanations uncritically; the reasons why people take their own lives are usually complex, with multiple factors interacting.

clause: People with suicidal intent can change their minds if human intervention at a late stage provides a spark of hope; intervention can be as simple as asking someone, "Are you OK?"
